title: Photochemical Reaction Lab: Robot-Assisted Light Exposure Analysis
description: In a virtual photochemistry lab, a robot assistant operates an antique camera repurposed as a high-intensity UV light source to trigger photochemical reactions in a series of solution vials. The user must configure wavelength, exposure duration, catalyst type, solution concentration, and beam angle parameters, then command the robot to aim the camera-light at each vial and validate the resulting color-change reactions match expected photochemical outcomes.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) implementing a photochemistry lab scene. Load 'shared_assets/robot.glb' on the left side as a lab assistant robot and 'shared_assets/AntiqueCamera.glb' mounted on a pivoting arm in front of the robot, repurposed as a UV light projector. Place 5 glass vials (transparent cylinder geometries with colored liquid inside using MeshPhysicalMaterial) on a lab bench (box geometry with wood texture) to the right. Add a control panel as an HTML overlay with: (1) wavelength slider 200-700nm, (2) exposure duration dropdown 1-10 seconds, (3) catalyst selector with options None/TiO2/ZnO/CdS, (4) concentration input 0.1-5.0 mol/L with validation, (5) beam angle slider 10-60 degrees, and (6) a target vial selector 1-5. Add a 'Fire Light' button. When clicked, validate all parameters are within range and chemically consistent (e.g., TiO2 requires wavelength <400nm). If valid, animate the robot rotating toward the selected vial, tilt the antique camera to aim at it, emit a visible cone light (SpotLight) from the camera lens matching the wavelength color, and change the vial liquid color to simulate the photochemical reaction result over the exposure duration. Each vial has a predefined correct parameter combination; display a floating check or X mark above each vial after exposure. Track completed reactions in a results log panel. Use OrbitControls for camera navigation. Add ambient light and a point light above the bench. The scene camera should start at position (0, 3, 6) looking at the bench center. Include a progress indicator showing how many of the 5 reactions are correctly completed. All 5 correct completions trigger a congratulatory message.
